name: Chromium nicotinate

lead: Chromium nicotinate is trace-mineral chromium bound to niacin, sold in supplements marketed for weight loss, muscle building and blood sugar. People take it for fewer cravings, better nutrient use and a leaner, more muscular look.

Chromium has been proposed to enhance insulin signaling, possibly through a chromium-binding peptide. Reviews of chromium supplements report no reliable evidence for body-weight effects, EFSA found evidence insufficient for body-weight claims, and a trial of chromium nicotinate in type 2 diabetes found no effect on insulin sensitivity. Most research covers picolinate rather than nicotinate.

paras: Taken orally as a daily supplement, often in multivitamin or fat-loss and body-composition stacks, alongside diet and training. Users judge results over weeks to months.

Little evidence of toxicity at typical amounts; rare allergic reactions, headache, insomnia and kidney or liver reports exist, mostly with picolinate. It may interact with medicines, including insulin.

angle.text: Chromium nicotinate is taken for fat loss, muscle gain and blood sugar control, on the idea that chromium improves how the body handles carbohydrate. Trials of chromium forms have measured body composition directly, with mixed results.

lead: Chromium nicotinate (chromium polynicotinate) is a form of trivalent chromium bound to niacin, sold as a dietary supplement alongside chromium picolinate and chromium chloride. Chromium products have been marketed for fat loss, muscle gain and blood sugar control [1][2].

Reviews cited by Wikipedia report no reliable evidence for body-weight effects: a 2013 Cochrane review found no reliable evidence on which to base firm decisions, and the European Food Safety Authority found evidence insufficient for body-weight claims [1]. A randomized trial of chromium nicotinate in people with type 2 diabetes found no effect on insulin sensitivity, glycemic control or lipids [3]. Most published work on chromium forms concerns picolinate rather than nicotinate.
infobox: Weight loss, body composition, glucose control [1]
Dietary supplement; EFSA found insufficient evidence for weight claims [1]

paras: Wikipedia notes that chromium was once proposed as essential for normal glucose handling, but that this role has not been sufficiently demonstrated, and that EFSA saw no convincing evidence of essentiality [1]. Several chromium forms are sold; Wikipedia states that picolinate is absorbed more efficiently than chloride or nicotinate [1]. The biologically active form of chromium is unknown [1].

Cell and animal work compared chromium forms. A 1992 study in cultured rat muscle cells found that chromium picolinate, but not chromium nicotinate or chloride, increased insulin internalization [4]. A 1997 rat study found that chromium nicotinate and other forms influenced blood pressure in spontaneously hypertensive rats [5]. A 1997 macrophage study compared oxidative stress induced by chromium picolinate and chromium nicotinate [6]. A 1995 study found chromosome damage in hamster ovary cells with chromium picolinate [7]; the UK Committee on Mutagenicity later concluded picolinate should be regarded as not mutagenic in vitro [1].

Wikipedia reports that typical supplemental amounts show little evidence of toxicity, but that adverse effects including allergic reactions, headache, insomnia and rare kidney or liver injury have been reported, mostly for picolinate [1]. Supplementation is not recommended in pregnancy [1].

A randomized trial found chromium nicotinate had no effect on insulin sensitivity, glycemic control or lipid profile in subjects with type 2 diabetes [3]. A trial of chromium supplementation in HIV-infected patients reported improved insulin resistance and metabolic abnormalities [8]. A 1997 study of chromium picolinate with exercise in obese women reported weight gain with supplementation alone [9]. A 2024 systematic review examined chromium supplementation in type 2 diabetes [10]. No published trial testing chromium nicotinate specifically for fat loss or appearance was found.
